pr_title: stream: pipeline should use req.abort() to destroy response
pr_body:
destroy(err) on http response will propagate the error to the
request causing 'error' to be unexpectedly emitted. Furthermore,
response.destroy() unlike request.abort() does not _dump buffered
data.

Fixes a breaking change applied in https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/648088289d619bfb149fe90316ce0127083c4c99.

Prefer res.req.abort() over res.destroy() until this situation is
clarified.

This is a bugfix and I believe it should be semver minor.

Fixes https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/31029.

issue_context.title: `stream.pipeline(httpResponse, decompressStream)` emits error three times
comments: Let's revert https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/648088289d619bfb149fe90316ce0127083c4c99 and try again - I'm swamped, it would be great if somebody else took care of it.

There's no need to revert that. I would just replace:

https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/648088289d619bfb149fe90316ce0127083c4c99/lib/internal/streams/pipeline.js#L46-L54

with

```js
    if (isRequest(stream.req)) return stream.req.abort();
    if (typeof stream.destroy === 'function') return stream.destroy(err);
```

The same is already done if you provide `ClientRequest` directly
(perhaps you just missed that, no worries):
https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/648088289d619bfb149fe90316ce0127083c4c99/lib/internal/streams/pipeline.js#L45

Yes, `res.destroy(err)` propagating the error to `req` might be a bit weird, though I'm actually not sure what is "correct" here. I'm working on trying to clarify these cases.

For now I think @szmarczak suggestion makes sense. @szmarczak would you like to create a PR? I'll investigate later whether that would have any impact on what https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/648088289d619bfb149fe90316ce0127083c4c99 was trying to fix.

review_comments: Does it make sense to also validate the error here?
I agree. At least that `err` is truthy.

Fixed. Unfortunately we get an unexpected/different error (`ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED`) due to the behavior discussed in https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/31060. So I made it just check for truthyness.
Bisecting points to 67ed526ab03c3e9b2f41290b7cd6e9c2e7d9b4dd.
@lpinca: The stream is `.destroyed` but `pipe` will continue writing causing a sync `ERR_STREAM_DESTOYRED` which will gain precedence.
It does not happen with Node.js 13.5.0

@lpinca: You are right. It doesn't have any async in destruction but since `write` [emits `ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED` sync](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/master/lib/_stream_writable.js#L323) (fixed in https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/29744) the problem is the same as if the writable had an async `_destroy` (in which case we are back here with the same "problem").

> It does not happen with Node.js 13.5.0

Yes, looks like Node 13.5.0 had another bug (probably related to `errorEmitted`) which would hide this.
Yes, again `git bisect` points to 67ed526ab03c3e9b2f41290b7cd6e9c2e7d9b4dd where the `errorEmitted` guard was moved to the same tick where the error is emitted.

> the problem is the same as if the writable had an async `_destroy` (in which case we are back here with the same "problem")

I disagree on this. The problem is not the same. In this case there is no ambiguity. `_destroy()` callback is called with an error (but the error is emitted later) **before** `writable.write()` is called. The `writable.write()` error should not be emitted as it occurred after the `destroy()` error.

> In this case there is no ambiguity.

Yes, if the write ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED error was async (as it should be) there would be no ambiguity.
Even if it is sync there is no ambiguity. In this case `writable.destroy()` is fully completed and with an error before `writable.write()` occurs.
write is called before the error is emitted since the error is emitted in a tick later

Yes, that's why the guard was set on destroy complete (before https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/67ed526ab03c3e9b2f41290b7cd6e9c2e7d9b4dd) instead of the actual tick where the error is emitted, I guess.
So ignore destroy with error after _destroy has completed. Is that another option to consider?
If that `_destroy()` completed with an error yes, totally.
Cool. I’ll add it to the proposals list.
How can this thread be resolved? We need a fix with the bug this PR aims to solve for node v13, or better revert the few commits that caused the problem in the first place.
I don't think this specific thread needs to be urgently resolved (or at the least it's a different issue). This PR in its current form resolves the original issue.
Agreed, this discussion should not block the PR. The issue discussed here is caused by a semver-major change that will not be included in v13.x
